title: Seedling SDK tours and checkpoint proposals
content:
Purpose
This is a working sketch for a lightweight, stage-based SDK onboarding experience we can A/B test. Focus is on reducing time-to-first-success and lowering cognitive load for engineers who are evaluating or integrating the Redwood SDK for inference (text, chat, embeddings). This doc captures the proposed "guided tours" concept, checkpoint milestones, minimal quickstart flows for web/CLI, instrumentation points, and a small experiment plan.

Audience and problem statement
- Primary audience: full‑stack and ML engineers evaluating Redwood in the first 1–4 hours.
- Secondary: platform engineers integrating SDKs into internal infra or CI templates.
- Problems we see today: long docs, multiple entry points (REST vs SDK vs CLI), unclear success signal (what counts as "it works"), and loss of momentum after initial setup friction.

Core idea: Guided tours + checklists
- Guided tour = a short, linear experience inside docs + sample repo that takes someone from zero to a verifiable success checkpoint in under 10 minutes. The tour should be modular and composable so we can surface bits in the console, docs, or interactive shell.
- Checkpoints = small, testable milestones with a clear success indicator (HTTP 200 + JSON schema match, embedding L2 distance < threshold in demo, or streamed token arrival). Each checkpoint will have a single screenshot/curl command as evidence.

Proposed checkpoints (order matters)
1) Authenticate: API key set, call to /v1/ping or minimal SDK call returns 200. Success indicator: console prints "connected: Redwood API vX".
2) Generate: run a two-line generator example that streams a short completion. Indicator: first streamed chunk arrives within 2s in local demo.
3) Chat turn: send a short multi-turn example; SDK shows message history preserved. Indicator: final chat response contains expected marker string (e.g. "REDWOOD_OK").
4) Embedding + search: index two sample docs, run a similarity query returning the correct doc as top hit. Indicator: top result id == "doc-1".
5) Telemetry observed: SDK emits minimal telemetry event and we display it in a dev console stub. Indicator: telemetry event with event_type "sdk.onboard.complete" visible.

Minimal quickstarts (two flavors)
A) Web quickstart (Javascript) — 6 steps, 5–8 minutes\- npm init + install @redwood/inference-sdk\- set REDWOOD_API_KEY env or browser-safe token (note: include note about CORS + ephemeral tokens)\- paste minimal app.js showing streaming generator to UI\- run dev server, open browser, confirm streaming chunks\- optional: wire simple debounced embedding search\- success: UI shows generated output and console prints telemetry event

B) CLI-first (Python) — 5 steps, 3–6 minutes\- pip install redwood-sdk\- set environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY
- run redwood quickstart-cli --mode=generator (script included)
- observe token stream in terminal
- run redwood embed-and-search sample with sample docs
- success: terminal prints top-hits table and telemetry visible in local stub

Guided tour UX components (where we host/implement)
- short-play doc page with embedded runnable code (CodeSandbox / Gitpod / Repl)\- companion sample-repo (tagged release) with tiny apps for both flows\- in-console "Try this" button that forks the sample into a browser-run environment or injects ephemeral credentials\- opt-in telemetry popup to show "how success is measured" and collect consent (GDPR-friendly)

Instrumentation and telemetry plan (minimal, privacy-first)
- Events to emit: sdk.started_tour, sdk.checkpoint_passed (checkpoint_id), sdk.tour_completed, sdk.sample_forked\- Data we capture: checkpoint_id, duration_ms, sdk_version, platform (node/python), anonymized_session_id\- Retention: index metrics aggregated weekly; raw session ids live for 7 days then drop. No code or user prompts in telemetry.

Experiment matrix (week 0–4)
- Variant A: current docs (control)\- Variant B: guided tour page + sample-repo + in-console "Try this"\- Variant C: B + ephemeral tokens to eliminate key setup friction
Metrics: time-to-checkpoint-1, tour-completion-rate, 24h return rate, repo-star/fork rate, support tickets opened during onboarding.

Developer notes / implementation checklist (MVP)
- create sample-repo with node + python folders (owner: Jonas)\- add short README with explicit success markers and screenshot assets (owner: Maya)\- console: add "Try guided tour" CTA (owner: Elena)\- docs: guided-tour page with embedded Repl and short paragraphs (owner: Rav i)
- implement minimal telemetry events in SDK cores (owner: eng-runtime team)\- privacy review with legal for ephemeral token flow (owner: security & compliance)

Open questions and risks
- Should we include rate-limited demo tokens publicly? (security: risk of abuse)
- How opinionated should the quickstart be about architecture? (keep it minimal, avoid rollout complexity)
- Do we require streaming for first success? Streaming shows latency benefits but can fail on some CI environments. Consider non-streaming fallback sample.
- Does telemetry interfere with corporate evals behind strict firewalls? Provide an opt-out and offline first flow.

Next steps (this week)
- sync 30m with Console PM to align on "Try guided tour" CTA placement (owner: Maya)\- create sample-repo skeleton and push initial commit (owner: Jonas)\- draft the docs page copy and 2 screenshots (owner: Ravi)

Notes to self / rough language snippets to use in the tour
- "First success goal: get one generated token and one embedding search result. If you see both, you can move to integration."
- "If you want a zero-key demo, click 'Run in sandbox' — this creates a short-lived token valid for 10 minutes."

Comments welcome. I'm leaving a few TODO flags inline in the sample-repo: TODO: add CI smoke test for checkpoint-1; TODO: add a non-streaming fallback example for CI.

Revision log
- 2025-02-14: initial sketch (Maya)\- 2025-02-18: added telemetry plan and experiment matrix (Ravi)\- 2025-03-05: clarified checkpoints and quickstart scripts (Elena)
